title: Model version anchoring, deterministic rollback, and resolution protocol for API/SDK
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Problem statement: As we onboard more community and partner models, customers need a clear, deterministic contract for selecting an exact model artifact via the Redwood API/SDK. Current selector behaviors (tag/semver/hash) are under-specified across layers: client SDK, control plane resolver, and serving runtime. This ticket defines a single unambiguous resolution protocol called the Version Anchoring Protocol (VAP) that supports: - pin-by-tag (release channel), - semver ranges (major.minor specification), - exact commit/hash pins, and - integrated performance-profile lookup for runtime optimization. The protocol must guarantee deterministic resolution, explain runtime fallback order, support auditability (resolution logs), and define safe rollback semantics for automated/controlled rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A prose spec for VAP that covers client, control-plane, and runtime responsibilities
SDK surface changes documented with examples for pin_by_tag, pin_by_semver, pin_by_hash
Control plane returns a single resolved artifact ref and an ordered fallback list with TTL and affinity metadata
Runtime honors the resolved ref, records resolution metadata in logs and metrics, and exposes it in request traces
Backward-compatible behavior for existing unpinned calls (default latest-stable) is documented
Automated end-to-end tests demonstrating deterministic resolution for 1000 random selector permutations
proposed_api: Summary of the API surface changes: 1) New optional field in model selection payload: 'anchor' which accepts an object encoded as a stringified selector expression. Examples: - anchor="tag:stable" - anchor="semver:^2.3" - anchor="hash:6f2a1b4c" 2) New top-level response fields: resolved_ref, resolution_reason, resolution_trace_id, fallback_chain (list of refs), resolution_ttl_seconds. 3) HTTP error 409 when selector is ambiguous and 'require_deterministic' header is set. Full JSON schema lives in the linked spec doc (Confluence).
runtime_resolution_matrix: Behavioral matrix summary: - Client provides anchor -> Control plane resolves authoritative artifact or returns ordered fallbacks. - If anchor is tag: control plane maps tag -> most recent matching stable artifact within tag window. - If anchor is semver range: control plane resolves highest semver satisfying range with policy awareness (experimental flags, deprecation windows). - If anchor is hash: control plane resolves exact artifact; if missing, return 404 unless allow_fallback is true. - If allow_fallback is true: control plane appends nearest compatible artifact(s) in fallback_chain with compatibility score and reason codes. - Runtime must accept resolved_ref and refuse to run if serving node lacks artifact unless runtime_fallback_policy allows substitution with recorded degradation reason.
rollback_and_fallback_behavior: Principles and protocol: 1) Deterministic rollback: when a model version needs rollback, the control plane will update tag mappings and emit a resolution-event with change_id. Clients that specify tag will deterministically pick up the new mapping; clients that pinned by hash will be unaffected. 2) Automatic fallback: three-tier fallback order: 1) exact resolved_ref, 2) compatible minor versions, 3) lightweight CPU-only fallback model (costly, last resort). Each fallback must include a degradation_score and customer-visible reason. 3) Safety gates: rollouts that change tag mappings automatically create a canary subgroup (5% of traffic); failed canaries trigger automatic re-anchoring to previous stable ref and postmortem ticket creation.
performance_profile_publishing: When a model artifact is published, its onboarding job must also create a performance profile record with keys: latency_p50, latency_p95, throughput_tokens_per_sec, mem_footprint_bytes, quantization_supported (true/false as string). The control plane exposes a model_performance endpoint; when resolving a selector, the resolver attaches the best-matching performance profile for the target hardware (found by region/instance-class mapping). SDKs will expose an optional prefer_profile_hint flag to request low-latency vs low-cost profiles.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize spec and API schema. Confluence spec published and reviewed by runtime, SDK, security.
Week 2: Implement control plane resolver + unit tests. Add resolution logs and metrics.exports.
Week 3: SDK surface changes (JS/Python/Go) + integration tests against staging resolver
Week 4: Runtime acceptance: honor resolved_ref, expose tracing headers, and verify fallback behavior in lab
Week 5: Canary rollout to 5% of hosted API traffic for non-critical models; collect metrics and run automatic checks
Week 6: Ramp to 100% for hosted API and publish migration guide for customers
test_plan: Deterministic resolver unit tests for tag/semver/hash combos
Integration tests exercises allow_fallback true/false and verifies runtime honors resolved_ref
Chaos tests: drop artifact on serving node and verify fallback_chain triggers and logs
Performance tests: ensure resolution latency < 10ms 99th percentile for cached lookups
E2E customer simulation: migrate 50 sandbox orgs to semver pins and verify no semantic regression
metrics_and_slo: Fallback usage rate < 0.5% in steady state
Canary failure detection within 15 minutes of rollout if degradation_score > 0.2
open_questions: How should we represent semver pre-release tags (alpha/beta) in tag windows?
What is the expected TTL for cached resolution entries per customer? (default 300s proposed)
Should we allow cross-model fallbacks (e.g., smaller family model) and how to articulate customer-facing cost/quality tradeoffs?
What level of sign-off is required for automatic re-anchoring after a failed canary (auto vs manual)
